title: Bienvenue dans notre école!
oneGoal: Students will identify their school as a special place and express feelings about being part of the school community

opening.activity: Welcome circle with school mascot or special object. Share excitement about being at school together.
materials: school mascot or special school symbol
opening.visualSupports: Big smile gestures, welcoming arms, photos of happy children at school

main.activity: School building appreciation walk. Stop at special places to notice what makes school feel welcoming. Return to create a 'Our School is Special' chart with drawings and words.
main.visualSupports: Point to building features, use appreciation gestures, encouraging facial expressions

decisionPoints.question: How familiar are students with their school building?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on deeper appreciation and feelings about familiar spaces
decisionPoints.ifNo: Take more time exploring and orienting students to school layout

decisionPoints.question: What level of emotional support do students need for school comfort?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use buddy system and extra reassurance about school safety
decisionPoints.ifNo: Encourage independent exploration and sharing of discoveries

closing.activity: Share one thing that makes our school special. Create class commitment to taking care of our special school.
closing.assessment: Observe student comfort level with school environment and ability to identify positive school features

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling nervous or uncertain about school
troubleshooting.then: Focus on safe, welcoming people and spaces. Use more reassurance and buddy support

realWorldConnection: Every person belongs to communities like school, family, and neighborhood

title: Je suis un élève
oneGoal: Students will understand their identity as students and recognize their rights and responsibilities in school

opening.activity: Mirror circle where students look at themselves and say 'Je suis un élève' (I am a student). Discuss what being a student means.
opening.visualSupports: Point to self proudly, student badge gestures, learning action poses

main.activity: Rights and responsibilities exploration through role-play scenarios. Act out student rights (safety, learning, respect) and responsibilities (kindness, effort, care). Create student rights and responsibilities poster.
main.visualSupports: Acting gestures for scenarios, thumbs up for rights, helping hands for responsibilities

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to discuss responsibilities or should we focus on rights first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance rights and responsibilities equally in discussion
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus heavily on rights first, then gently introduce responsibilities

decisionPoints.question: How do we balance individual identity with group belonging?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize both 'I am special' and 'We belong together'
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus more on individual identity and comfort first

closing.activity: Student identity celebration where each child receives recognition for being an important student in our class.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of student role and comfort with rights/responsibilities concepts

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused about abstract concepts like rights and responsibilities
troubleshooting.then: Use more concrete examples and role-play. Focus on specific situations they experience daily

realWorldConnection: Being a student is an important role with special rights and responsibilities

title: Notre salle de classe
oneGoal: Students will explore their classroom space and understand how spaces are organized for learning and community

opening.activity: Classroom space appreciation tour. Students become 'space detectives' looking for different areas and their purposes.
opening.visualSupports: Detective gestures, pointing to different areas, questioning expressions

main.activity: Classroom mapping activity. Students work in pairs to create simple maps of classroom areas. Identify learning spaces, quiet spaces, group spaces. Share maps and explain favorite areas.
main.visualSupports: Bird's eye view gestures, mapping motions, labeling actions

decisionPoints.question: Which classroom areas are most meaningful for students to explore?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on student-chosen areas and their personal connections
decisionPoints.ifNo: Guide exploration to ensure all functional areas are understood

decisionPoints.question: Should we create a classroom map together or individually?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create individual maps first, then combine into class map
decisionPoints.ifNo: Work together on one large class map with everyone contributing

closing.activity: Classroom space commitment circle. Students share how they will take care of different classroom areas.
closing.assessment: Observe student spatial awareness and understanding of how space organization supports learning

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty with mapping concepts
troubleshooting.then: Use floor-level perspective first, then gradually introduce bird's eye view with physical examples

realWorldConnection: All learning spaces are designed to help people work, learn, and be together

title: Les espaces de notre école
oneGoal: Students will identify different school spaces and understand how each space serves the school community

opening.activity: School space picture walk. Show photos of different school areas and have students predict what happens in each space.
opening.visualSupports: Point to photos clearly, use wondering gestures, prediction thinking poses

main.activity: School exploration walking tour. Visit library, gymnasium, cafeteria, office, music room. At each space, observe activities and interview people about how the space serves the school community. Record discoveries on exploration sheets.
main.visualSupports: Observation gestures, respectful visiting behavior, note-taking actions

decisionPoints.question: Which school spaces are most important for students to understand first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Prioritize spaces students use regularly (library, gym, cafeteria)
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include spaces students rarely see (boiler room, storage) for broader understanding

decisionPoints.question: Should we take a walking tour or use photos and maps?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine walking tour with photo documentation for later reference
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use virtual tour approach with photos, videos, and maps

closing.activity: School spaces appreciation circle. Share discoveries about how different spaces help our school community.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of space-function relationships and community service concepts

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by large school building or getting distracted during tour
troubleshooting.then: Visit fewer spaces with more focused attention, or use virtual tour approach with photos

realWorldConnection: Different spaces in our community serve different purposes for different people

title: Notre directeur et secrétaire
oneGoal: Students will understand the roles of principal and secretary in supporting the school community

opening.activity: Role guessing game. Act out different jobs and have students guess. Introduce principal and secretary roles through mime and photos.
opening.visualSupports: Clear job action gestures, office work motions, helping others poses

main.activity: Office visit and interview session. Visit school office to meet principal and secretary. Conduct prepared interview about their roles in helping students and teachers. Observe office work and ask questions about how they support school community.
main.visualSupports: Respectful visiting posture, listening gestures, questioning hand raises

decisionPoints.question: How comfortable are students with meeting school authority figures?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage natural conversation and questions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use more structured interview format with prepared questions

decisionPoints.question: Should we visit the office or invite guests to our classroom?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Office visit gives authentic context for understanding their work
decisionPoints.ifNo: Classroom visit might feel safer and more controlled for students

closing.activity: Thank you card creation for principal and secretary. Share appreciation for how they help our school community.
closing.assessment: Observe student understanding of leadership roles and comfort with school authority figures

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students intimidated by principal or office environment
troubleshooting.then: Focus on friendly, helping aspects of roles. Use photos and stories before any direct meeting

realWorldConnection: Every community has leaders who help organize and support everyone

title: Nos enseignants et aide-enseignants
oneGoal: Students will recognize teaching roles and understand how educators support student learning and growth

opening.activity: Teacher appreciation discussion. Share what students notice about how teachers help them learn and feel cared for.
opening.visualSupports: Caring gestures, helping hand motions, learning support actions

main.activity: Teacher and aide-enseignant interview project. Students prepare questions about why people become teachers and how they help students. Interview classroom teacher, aide-enseignant, and other school teachers. Learn about teachers' interests, families, and reasons for loving teaching.
main.visualSupports: Interview posture, respectful listening, note-taking gestures

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students see teachers as people with feelings and needs?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include questions about teachers' lives, interests, and experiences
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on professional roles and classroom responsibilities

decisionPoints.question: Should we interview teachers or observe them in action?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine interviews with classroom observation of teaching in action
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on interview format to encourage personal connection

closing.activity: Teacher appreciation creation. Make thank you notes or drawings expressing gratitude for how teachers support learning.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of teaching roles and ability to appreciate educator contributions

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students struggling to think of meaningful interview questions
troubleshooting.then: Provide question starters and model questioning. Focus on what students are curious about

realWorldConnection: Teachers and helpers exist in many community settings, not just schools

title: Le concierge et la cuisine
oneGoal: Students will appreciate support staff roles and understand how everyone contributes to school community

opening.activity: Community helpers appreciation circle. Discuss all the people who help make school work, focusing on often-overlooked support roles.
opening.visualSupports: Work action gestures, appreciation expressions, community helper poses

main.activity: Support staff appreciation interviews and observations. Visit custodial areas and kitchen (if possible) to observe support staff work. Interview custodian about keeping school clean and safe. Meet kitchen staff and learn about feeding school community. Understand how support work keeps school functioning.
main.visualSupports: Work observation gestures, respectful visiting behavior, appreciation expressions

decisionPoints.question: How do we highlight the importance of support roles without stereotyping?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Emphasize skill, importance, and choice in all work roles
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on appreciation without discussing role value comparisons

decisionPoints.question: Should we observe work in action or have conversations with staff?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine observation with conversation for full understanding
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on conversation to build personal connections with staff

closing.activity: Support staff thank you project. Create appreciation gifts or notes recognizing essential work of custodial and kitchen staff.
closing.assessment: Observe student appreciation for diverse work roles and understanding of community interdependence

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not understanding importance of support roles
troubleshooting.then: Use 'what if' scenarios - what if no one cleaned, cooked, or maintained school?

realWorldConnection: Every community depends on people who maintain spaces and provide services

title: Les règles de notre école
oneGoal: Students will understand school rules as community agreements that help everyone feel safe and included

opening.activity: Rule exploration through scenarios. Present situations and discuss what rules might help everyone feel safe and happy.
opening.visualSupports: Safety gestures, problem-solving expressions, community cooperation poses

main.activity: School rule investigation project. Explore different areas of school to discover existing rules (posted signs, common practices). Interview staff about why certain rules exist. Discuss how rules help community function. Create illustrated rule book showing how rules help everyone.
main.visualSupports: Rule reading gestures, safety demonstrations, community agreement actions

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to discuss rule purposes or should we focus on examples first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore both what rules are and why they exist
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on identifying and understanding existing rules first

decisionPoints.question: Should we create new class rules or explore existing school rules?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine exploration of existing rules with collaborative creation of class agreements
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on understanding and appreciating existing school rule system

closing.activity: Rule commitment ceremony. Students share how they will follow school rules to help everyone feel safe and included.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of rule purposes and commitment to community agreements

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students seeing rules as restrictive rather than helpful
troubleshooting.then: Use more positive framing - 'rules help us' rather than 'rules stop us'. Focus on safety and inclusion benefits

realWorldConnection: All communities have agreements that help people live and work together safely

title: Comment nous résolvons les problèmes
oneGoal: Students will practice conflict resolution and understand how to seek help when problems arise

opening.activity: Problem-solving warm-up. Present simple classroom problems and brainstorm solutions together.
opening.visualSupports: Thinking gestures, problem-solving expressions, solution discovery actions

main.activity: Conflict resolution skill building through role-play. Practice common student conflicts (sharing, fairness, feelings). Learn steps: stop, breathe, talk, listen, solve together. Practice seeking help from adults when needed. Create problem-solving poster for classroom reference.
main.visualSupports: Calm-down gestures, talking and listening poses, helping hand signals

decisionPoints.question: What types of conflicts are most relevant to students' experience?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on conflicts students actually experience in classroom and playground
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use hypothetical scenarios to introduce problem-solving concepts

decisionPoints.question: Should we role-play solutions or discuss real classroom situations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Carefully address real situations that have occurred with sensitivity
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use role-play scenarios to practice skills without personalizing conflicts

closing.activity: Problem-solving commitment circle. Students share one problem-solving strategy they will try when conflicts arise.
closing.assessment: Observe student understanding of conflict resolution steps and comfort with help-seeking

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students getting upset during conflict role-play or real situation discussion
troubleshooting.then: Use more abstract scenarios, focus on positive solutions, provide extra emotional support

realWorldConnection: Learning to solve problems peacefully helps in all relationships and communities

title: Nos traditions scolaires
oneGoal: Students will explore school traditions and understand how shared experiences build community identity

opening.activity: Tradition introduction through storytelling. Share stories about special things the school does every year that make it unique.
opening.visualSupports: Story gestures, celebration actions, tradition demonstration poses

main.activity: School tradition exploration project. Research school traditions through photos, artifacts, and interviews with long-time staff. Learn about assemblies, special events, annual celebrations. Understand how traditions connect past and present school community. Create tradition timeline or museum display.
main.visualSupports: Historical comparison gestures, timeline actions, celebration demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Which school traditions are most meaningful for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on traditions students can participate in and understand
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include broader school traditions to build comprehensive understanding

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on current year traditions or school history?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance current traditions students will experience with historical context
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on traditions students will directly participate in this year

closing.activity: Tradition appreciation circle. Students share excitement about school traditions they want to participate in.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of tradition purposes and excitement about school community participation

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students from different cultural backgrounds feeling excluded from school traditions
troubleshooting.then: Explicitly discuss how diverse traditions enrich school community. Invite sharing of family traditions

realWorldConnection: Traditions help communities remember their values and celebrate together

title: Ma carte de l'école
oneGoal: Students will create simple maps of school spaces and understand how maps help us navigate community spaces

opening.activity: Map exploration introduction. Look at different types of maps and discuss how they help people find their way.
opening.visualSupports: Map reading gestures, direction pointing, navigation actions

main.activity: School mapping project. Students create individual maps of school layout, marking important spaces and pathways. Include favorite spots, important rooms, and safety locations. Add symbols and labels. Share maps and compare different perspectives and details noticed.
main.visualSupports: Bird's eye view demonstrations, mapping motions, symbol explanation gestures

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for bird's-eye view mapping or should we use floor-level perspective?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce bird's eye view with physical demonstrations and examples
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with floor-level perspective and gradually introduce aerial view concepts

decisionPoints.question: Should maps focus on favorite spaces or all school areas?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage personal mapping with favorite spaces highlighted
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide structure for comprehensive school area mapping

closing.activity: Map gallery walk. Students display maps and explain special features they included. Appreciate different mapping perspectives.
closing.assessment: Observe student spatial awareness, mapping skills, and ability to represent three-dimensional space

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students frustrated with mapping complexity or accuracy
troubleshooting.then: Focus on creative representation rather than accuracy. Emphasize personal meaning over technical precision

realWorldConnection: Maps help us understand and navigate all the communities we belong to

title: Interview avec le personnel
oneGoal: Students will conduct simple interviews with school staff to understand their roles and contributions

opening.activity: Interview skill practice. Learn how to ask good questions, listen carefully, and show appreciation for people's answers.
opening.visualSupports: Question asking gestures, careful listening poses, note-taking actions

main.activity: School staff interview project. Students work in pairs to interview different school staff members they haven't met yet (music teacher, librarian, special education teacher, etc.). Ask about their roles, why they chose their job, how they help students. Record answers through drawings and simple words. Share discoveries with class.
main.visualSupports: Professional interview posture, respectful questioning, note-taking demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Which staff members would be most comfortable and engaging for student interviews?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose staff known for enjoying student interaction and communication
decisionPoints.ifNo: Prepare staff in advance and provide structured interview formats

decisionPoints.question: Should interviews be structured with prepared questions or more conversational?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use structured questions to build student confidence and focus
decisionPoints.ifNo: Encourage natural conversation with question prompts available

closing.activity: Interview discovery sharing. Students share interesting things they learned about school staff and their contributions to school community.
closing.assessment: Note student questioning skills, listening abilities, and understanding of diverse school roles

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students too shy or nervous to conduct interviews
troubleshooting.then: Use buddy system, practice with familiar adults first, or allow observation-based learning

realWorldConnection: Asking questions and listening to answers helps us understand our community better

title: Les besoins de notre école
oneGoal: Students will identify school community needs and understand how needs are met through cooperation

opening.activity: Needs vs. wants exploration. Discuss difference between things we need and things we want, using personal examples.
opening.visualSupports: Essential need gestures, want desire expressions, sorting actions

main.activity: School needs assessment project. Walk through school to identify what the school community needs to function well (safety, cleanliness, learning materials, kindness, cooperation). Distinguish between material needs and social/emotional needs. Interview staff about current school needs. Brainstorm how needs are currently met and how students can help.
main.visualSupports: Needs identification gestures, assessment actions, brainstorming thinking poses

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students distinguish between wants and needs in school context?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use concrete examples and 'what if' scenarios to clarify essential vs. nice-to-have
decisionPoints.ifNo: Accept broader interpretation of needs and focus on community cooperation

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on material needs or emotional/social needs first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with tangible material needs, then explore social/emotional community needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Integrate both types of needs as equally important for school community

closing.activity: School needs commitment circle. Students choose one school need they want to help address and share their commitment.
closing.assessment: Observe student understanding of community needs and readiness to contribute solutions

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students identifying too many wants as needs or feeling overwhelmed by school needs
troubleshooting.then: Focus on basic essential needs and emphasize how well current needs are already being met

realWorldConnection: All communities have needs that are met when people work together

title: Comment nous aidons notre école
oneGoal: Students will identify ways they can contribute to school community and take action to help

opening.activity: Helper appreciation circle. Discuss ways students already help at school and home. Celebrate existing contributions.
opening.visualSupports: Helping action demonstrations, appreciation expressions, contribution celebration gestures

main.activity: School contribution action project. Choose specific ways students can help school community based on needs identified in previous lesson. Implement helping actions: classroom organization, playground cleanup, kindness notes, buddy helping, office assistance. Document contributions through photos and reflections.
main.visualSupports: Helping action demonstrations, teamwork gestures, pride in contribution expressions

decisionPoints.question: What level of responsibility are students ready to take on?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Offer substantial helping opportunities with appropriate supervision
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with simple, manageable helping tasks to build confidence

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on individual contributions or group projects?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance individual choice with collaborative group helping projects
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on group projects to build community cooperation skills

closing.activity: Contribution celebration circle. Students share how it felt to help school community and plan continued contributions.
closing.assessment: Note student engagement in helping activities and understanding of community contribution

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling overwhelmed by responsibility or not seeing impact of their help
troubleshooting.then: Focus on small, immediately visible contributions. Celebrate all efforts enthusiastically

realWorldConnection: Everyone, including children, can make important contributions to their communities

title: Notre école dans le quartier
oneGoal: Students will understand their school's place in the larger neighborhood community

opening.activity: Neighborhood exploration introduction. Look at school location on maps and discuss what surrounds the school.
opening.visualSupports: Map pointing gestures, location identification actions, neighborhood connection expressions

main.activity: School-community connection exploration. From classroom windows and school boundaries, observe neighborhood features. Identify community connections (nearby businesses, homes, other schools, parks). Interview staff about school's role in neighborhood. Create community connection map showing school's place in larger community.
main.visualSupports: Observation pointing, community connection gestures, mapping demonstration actions

decisionPoints.question: How familiar are students with the area around their school?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Build on existing knowledge to deepen community understanding
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide foundational orientation to immediate school neighborhood

decisionPoints.question: Should we explore through windows, walks, or maps and photos?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine multiple exploration methods for comprehensive understanding
decisionPoints.ifNo: Choose safest and most practical exploration method for student group

closing.activity: School-community appreciation circle. Students share connections they discovered between school and neighborhood.
closing.assessment: Observe student understanding of school's place in larger community context

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students not seeing connections between school and neighborhood or feeling confused about community boundaries
troubleshooting.then: Use more concrete examples and visual aids. Focus on obvious, immediate connections first

realWorldConnection: Schools are part of larger communities with connections to many other places and people

title: Les écoles d'hier et d'aujourd'hui
oneGoal: Students will compare past and present schools and understand how communities change over time

opening.activity: Time travel introduction. Use props and storytelling to introduce concept of schools from long ago compared to today.
opening.visualSupports: Time passage gestures, historical comparison expressions, then/now demonstration actions

main.activity: School history exploration project. Compare historical photos of schools with current school. Interview older community members or staff about how schools have changed. Explore differences in classrooms, technology, activities, rules. Create then/now comparison display showing school community changes over time.
main.visualSupports: Historical comparison gestures, time difference demonstrations, change explanation actions

decisionPoints.question: What aspects of school history will be most interesting and accessible to Grade 1s?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on tangible differences students can observe and understand
decisionPoints.ifNo: Include broader historical context about education and community changes

decisionPoints.question: Should we use photos, artifacts, or stories from older community members?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Combine multiple sources for rich historical understanding
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on most engaging and accessible historical source for student group

closing.activity: Time appreciation circle. Students share what they appreciate about schools today and what was interesting about schools in the past.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of change over time and appreciation for historical and current school communities

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students confused about time concepts or overwhelmed by historical information
troubleshooting.then: Use simpler time comparisons. Focus on obvious, concrete differences students can easily understand

realWorldConnection: All communities have histories that help us understand how they became what they are today

title: Créer ensemble un projet d'école
oneGoal: Students will collaborate on a project that improves their school community

opening.activity: Project planning circle. Review school needs identified earlier and brainstorm manageable improvement projects students can complete together.
opening.visualSupports: Brainstorming thinking gestures, collaboration planning actions, project excitement expressions

main.activity: Community improvement project implementation. Work together on chosen project (classroom library organization, playground beautification, kindness campaign, school garden care, office helper program). Divide responsibilities, collaborate on execution, document process and impact.
materials: project supplies specific to chosen project
main.visualSupports: Teamwork cooperation gestures, project work demonstrations, progress celebration actions

decisionPoints.question: What type of project would be meaningful and achievable for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose project that provides visible impact and matches student developmental capabilities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Select simpler project that ensures success and builds confidence in community contribution

decisionPoints.question: Should the project focus on classroom, school, or neighborhood improvement?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose scope that allows students to see direct impact of their work
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on immediate school community for most meaningful and visible results

closing.activity: Project completion celebration. Admire completed project and discuss how collaboration made improvement possible.
closing.assessment: Observe student collaboration skills, project engagement, and understanding of community improvement

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students having difficulty with collaboration or project feeling too complex
troubleshooting.then: Simplify project scope, provide more structure for collaboration, celebrate small progress steps

realWorldConnection: Working together on projects is how communities solve problems and create positive changes

title: Présenter notre école
oneGoal: Students will share their school community knowledge with others and practice being school ambassadors

opening.activity: School ambassador preparation. Discuss how to share positive information about school with others. Practice confident, welcoming presentation skills.
opening.visualSupports: Confident presentation postures, welcoming gestures, information sharing actions

main.activity: School presentation project. Prepare and deliver presentations about school community to chosen audience (parents, other classes, potential new students, community members). Include information about school spaces, people, traditions, and why school is special. Use drawings, photos, maps, and spoken explanations.
main.visualSupports: Presentation delivery gestures, audience engagement actions, information sharing demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: Who would be the best audience for student presentations about their school?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose audience that will be genuinely interested and supportive
decisionPoints.ifNo: Present to classmates or teachers if external audience isn't available

decisionPoints.question: Should presentations be formal or conversational, individual or group?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Match presentation format to student comfort levels and learning goals
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use group presentations to provide mutual support and shared responsibility

closing.activity: Ambassador appreciation circle. Celebrate student success in representing their school community and sharing their knowledge.
closing.assessment: Note student confidence in sharing school knowledge and ability to represent school community positively

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students feeling nervous about presentations or struggling to organize information
troubleshooting.then: Provide more structure and support. Use group presentations or allow alternative sharing formats

realWorldConnection: Being able to describe and represent our communities helps others understand and appreciate them

title: Notre célébration scolaire
oneGoal: Students will plan and participate in a celebration that honors their school community

opening.activity: Celebration planning circle. Discuss different ways communities celebrate and appreciate each other. Brainstorm celebration ideas for school community.
opening.visualSupports: Celebration planning gestures, joyful expressions, community appreciation actions

main.activity: School community celebration event. Implement planned celebration that honors school community (appreciation assembly, thank you note delivery, community helper recognition, school pride display, gratitude ceremony). Include all school community members and focus on shared appreciation and belonging.
materials: celebration supplies based on chosen format
main.visualSupports: Celebration participation gestures, appreciation expressions, community joy demonstrations

decisionPoints.question: What format of celebration would best honor the diverse contributions in school community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Choose inclusive celebration format that recognizes many different contributions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple appreciation format that ensures everyone feels included

decisionPoints.question: Should celebration focus on students, staff, or the whole school community?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include whole school community to emphasize interconnected relationships
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on group that would be most meaningful and manageable for Grade 1 students

closing.activity: Celebration reflection circle. Share feelings about celebration and appreciation for school community relationships.
closing.assessment: Observe student joy in community celebration and understanding of appreciation expression

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students overwhelmed by celebration planning or execution
troubleshooting.then: Simplify celebration format, focus on genuine appreciation rather than elaborate activities

realWorldConnection: Celebrations help communities appreciate their shared experiences and values

title: Moi, élève et citoyen
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their growth as school community members and set goals for continued contribution

opening.activity: Growth reflection introduction. Look at documentation from throughout unit to see learning journey and community understanding development.
opening.visualSupports: Growth demonstration gestures, journey reflection actions, learning appreciation expressions

main.activity: School citizenship reflection project. Create personal reflection portfolio showing growth in understanding school community, roles, relationships, and contribution. Set goals for continued school citizenship. Plan ways to keep contributing to school community. Share reflections and goals with school community members.
main.visualSupports: Reflection thinking poses, goal setting actions, citizenship demonstration gestures

decisionPoints.question: How do we help students see their learning journey and growth over the unit?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use concrete examples and documentation to show visible learning progression
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on current understanding and abilities rather than change over time

decisionPoints.question: Should reflection focus on personal growth or community contribution?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance both personal learning and community impact in reflection
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on area that feels most meaningful and achievable for student group

closing.activity: School citizenship commitment ceremony. Students make commitments to continued positive school community membership and receive recognition as valued school citizens.
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of citizenship concepts and commitment to ongoing community contribution

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: Students struggling with abstract citizenship concepts or goal setting
troubleshooting.then: Use concrete examples of good school community membership. Focus on specific, achievable goals

realWorldConnection: Being a good community member is a lifelong journey of learning, contributing, and growing
